sources.title: Is the Great Wall of China really visible from space?
sources.excerpt: Is the Great Wall of China really visible from space? Contrary to popular belief, the

reasoning: The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye is a well-documented myth. In reality, the Great Wall is only a few meters wide and constructed from materials that blend into the surrounding terrain, making it virtually impossible to resolve with the unaided human eye from low Earth orbit (and completely impossible from the Moon). Astronauts and space agencies have confirmed that the wall requires optical magnification or specific lighting conditions to be photographed or detected, whereas other human-made structures—such as major highways, large airports, canals, and city lights at night—are far more visible from orbit.
